kinkajou: A kinkajou hanging from a branch by its long prehensile tail, a small round-bodied animal with a short blunt muzzle, a rounded head, very large dark eyes and small round ears set low on the sides of the head, covered in golden-brown woolly fur. Round-faced and teddy-bear-like, not a pointed-faced squirrel
ringtail: A ringtail, slender grey-brown body, large dark eyes, long bushy black-and-white ringed tail, perched on a rocky ledge
giantotter: A giant otter on all four legs, an extremely long-bodied otter with a very long thick muscular tail flattening into a wide paddle at the end, short stubby legs, large webbed feet, a broad flattened head with a blunt muzzle and small ears, sleek dark brown fur and a cream throat patch. Very long and low to the ground
seaotter: A sea otter, dense brown fur, round face with whiskers, floating on its back holding its paws to its chest
wolverine: A wolverine on all four legs, a low stocky bear-like mustelid with a broad heavy body slung low between short powerful legs, huge paws, a short broad blunt muzzle and small rounded ears, thick dark brown fur with a pale stripe sweeping along each side, and a short bushy tail. Squat and bear-like, not a wolf and not a long-legged dog
marten: A pine marten, rich brown fur with a cream-yellow throat patch, bushy tail, climbing a tree trunk
fisher: A fisher on all four legs, a long low weasel-shaped animal with a very elongated tube-like body and very short legs so its belly runs close to the ground, a small triangular head with a pointed muzzle and low rounded ears, dark glossy brown fur and a long bushy tail. Long and low like a giant weasel, not a dog
stoat: A stoat on all four legs, an extremely long and low weasel with a slender tube-shaped body, very short little legs, a small flat triangular head with tiny rounded ears, reddish-brown fur with a crisp white underside and a black-tipped tail. Long and low to the ground, not a leggy cat
weasel: A least weasel on all four legs with its long thin tube-like body held low and horizontal close to the ground, extremely short little legs, a tiny flat head with small rounded ears, brown fur with a white belly and a very short tail. Low and horizontal on four legs, not rearing up on its hind legs and not standing upright like a person
ferret: A black-footed ferret, pale buff fur with a black facial mask and black feet, standing on all four legs
mink: An American mink, sleek dark brown glossy fur, small white chin patch, standing on all four legs
tayra: A tayra on all four legs, a long low mustelid with an elongated body, short legs, a small flattened head with a pointed muzzle and low rounded ears, dark brown-black fur with a pale patch on the chest, and a long bushy tail. Long and low like a big weasel, not a dog
skunk: A striped skunk, black fur with two bold white stripes running down the back, bushy tail raised, standing on all four legs
gorilla: A gorilla, a massive black-furred ape in knuckle-walking posture seen from the side, its front knuckles resting on the ground, its back sloping down from high heavy shoulders to lower hips, head carried low and forward. An animal moving on four limbs, not standing upright, no human posture, no upright torso.
chimpanzee: A chimpanzee, black-furred body, bare expressive face, long arms, standing on all fours on a forest floor
bonobo: A bonobo, slender black-furred body, pink lips, parted long hair on the head, standing upright briefly on two legs
orangutan: An orangutan, a heavy shaggy reddish-orange ape moving on all fours seen from the side, its very long arms reaching the ground with the knuckles down, back roughly level, broad flat cheek-padded face. An animal on four limbs, not standing upright, no human posture.
gibbon: A white-handed gibbon, black fur with white hands and feet and a white face ring, swinging from a branch with long arms
siamang: A siamang hanging from a branch by one long arm, an all-black shaggy ape with a large inflated grey throat pouch ballooning out under its chin, very long slender arms and a small rounded pot-bellied ape torso. An ape body with no human musculature: no human chest, no abdominal muscles, not a muscular human figure
mandrill: A mandrill on all fours, a heavy stocky ground monkey with a compact barrel-shaped body, short thick limbs, a steeply sloping back and a tiny stub of a tail held upright, olive-brown fur, a vivid blue and red ridged muzzle and a golden beard. Stocky and compact on four legs, not a long-bodied lion or cat shape
baboon: An olive baboon, coarse olive-grey fur, elongated doglike muzzle, walking on all fours
gelada: A gelada on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with shaggy brown fur, a bare pink hourglass-shaped patch of skin on its chest, and tufted eyebrows
macaque: A rhesus macaque on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with brown-grey fur, a pink face and a short tail
capuchin: A tufted capuchin, black and buff fur, tuft of dark fur atop the head, prehensile tail curled, standing on all four legs
howler: A red howler monkey on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with reddish-orange shaggy fur, a deep bearded jaw and a thick prehensile tail curling behind it
spidermonkey: A spider monkey, long-limbed black fur, small head, long prehensile tail, hanging from a branch by its tail
marmoset: A common marmoset, mottled grey-brown fur, prominent white ear tufts, tiny body, clinging to a branch
tamarin: A golden lion tamarin on all four legs crouched along a branch and gripping it with all four hands, a tiny squirrel-sized monkey with vivid golden-orange silky fur and a spectacular full lion-like mane of long fur standing out all around its small dark bare face. On all fours on the branch, not standing upright on two legs and not holding a stick or a staff
colobus: A black-and-white colobus, glossy black fur with a white mantle and a long white-tufted tail, standing on all four legs
langur: A gray langur resting on all fours on the ground, a slender long-limbed monkey with silvery-grey fur, a black face and black hands, and a very long tail curving behind it. A slim monkey body with no human musculature: not an upright human figure and not sitting with its hands folded in its lap like a person
proboscis: A proboscis monkey on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with reddish-brown fur, a pale belly, a pot-bellied torso and an enormous drooping pendulous nose hanging down over its mouth like a long fleshy teardrop
uakari: A bald uakari on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with shaggy reddish-orange fur, a completely bald bright crimson-red face and a short stumpy tail
vervet: A vervet monkey on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with grizzled grey-olive fur, a black face framed by white fur and a long tail
snubnosed: A golden snub-nosed monkey on all fours with both hands and both feet flat on the ground, a barrel-shaped monkey torso and a back sloping from high shoulders, head carried low and forward. It is an animal on four legs: not an upright human figure, no human chest, no abdominal muscles, no bodybuilder physique, not standing on two legs, with long golden-orange fur and a flat pale blue face with a small upturned nose
ringtaillemur: A ring-tailed lemur standing on all four legs, with soft pale grey fur over the back shading to a warm grey-brown rump, a clean white underside, chest and limbs, and a striking white face marked with bold black triangular patches around each bright orange eye and a slender pointed jet-BLACK fox-like muzzle. Its long tail is held curled upright and is ringed along its whole length with many alternating black and white bands, about thirteen of each, narrow and evenly spaced. The black muzzle and the many narrow tail rings are essential
indri: An indri, black and white patchy fur, very short tail, large expressive eyes, gripping a vertical tree trunk
sifaka: A Verreaux's sifaka, white silky fur with a dark cap and chest patch, long tail, clinging upright to a tree trunk
ayeaye: An aye-aye clinging to a tree branch with all four hands at night, a lemur with shaggy dark brown fur, huge round orange eyes, very large thin rounded ears, a long bushy tail, and one extremely thin skeletal elongated middle finger on each hand. It is a lemur and has NO wings of any kind: no wing membranes, no bat wings, nothing spread behind it. It must not resemble a bat, and it is not standing upright holding a stick
tarsier: A Philippine tarsier, small brown-grey furred body, enormous round eyes far larger than its face proportionally, long fingers, clinging to a branch
loris: A slow loris clinging to a branch with all four hands wrapped tightly around it, a small round-bodied primate with dense grey-brown fur, huge round forward-facing eyes ringed with dark patches, tiny ears and no tail. Gripping the branch with all four hands held close to its body, not standing upright on two legs and not holding a stick or a staff
kangaroo: A red kangaroo seen from the side, reddish-tan fur, resting back on its powerful hind legs with its thick tail on the ground forming a tripod, small forelimbs hanging loosely near the chest, long muzzle and tall ears. An animal, not humanoid, no human torso, no hands on hips.
wallaby: A red-necked wallaby resting on its hind legs with its body leaning well forward and its thick heavy tail laid on the ground behind as a third support, small forepaws held close to its chest, a small deer-like head with long ears, grey-brown fur with a reddish nape. An animal leaning forward balanced by its tail, not an upright human figure with a human chest and human arms
treekangaroo: A tree kangaroo clinging to a tree trunk with all four limbs wrapped around it, boldly TWO-TONE in colour: a dark rich chestnut-mahogany brown back, shoulders and crown, contrasting sharply against a bright golden-yellow face, throat, chest, belly, forelimbs, feet and a long golden-yellow tail, the two colours meeting in a clear line along its flanks. Short rounded ears and a heavy tail hanging down. The bright golden-yellow underparts and tail are essential and it must not be a plain uniform reddish-brown animal
koala: A koala, dense grey fur, large round fluffy ears, big black spoon-shaped nose, clinging high on an upright tree trunk with all four paws wrapped around the trunk and its body pressed against it. It holds nothing in its paws, is not standing on the ground, and is not humanoid.
wombat: A common wombat, stocky brown-furred body, short legs, broad flat head, standing on all fours on grass
quokka: A quokka, small round-bodied brown fur, short round ears, rounded face with a permanent smile, standing on all four legs
tasdevil: A Tasmanian devil on all four legs, a squat compact animal the size of a small dog with a very large broad head that looks too big for its body, a thick neck, short stumpy legs, a stocky low body and a thick tapering tail, black fur with a white band across the chest. Small squat and heavy-headed, not a tall leggy black dog and not a panther
quoll: A spotted-tailed quoll, brown fur covered in white spots extending onto the tail, pointed snout, standing on all four legs
numbat: A numbat, reddish-brown fur with white stripes across the back, long bushy tail, long snout, standing on all four legs
bilby: A greater bilby, soft blue-grey fur, very large rabbit-like ears, long pointed snout, long black-and-white tail, standing on all four legs
bandicoot: An eastern barred bandicoot, greyish-brown fur with pale bars across the hindquarters, pointed snout, standing on all four legs
sugarglider: A sugar glider, soft grey fur with a dark dorsal stripe, large eyes, gliding membrane visible along its sides, clinging to a branch
cuscus: A spotted cuscus clinging to a branch with all four hands, a slow round-bodied possum with dense woolly white fur patched with brown-grey, a small round head with a short blunt face, small hidden ears, large round eyes and a thick curling prehensile tail. Round and slow-moving, not a slender weasel, and not holding a stick
opossum: A Virginia opossum, coarse grey-white fur, pointed pink snout, hairless prehensile tail, standing on all fours
zebra: A plains zebra, bold black and white striped body, standing on all four legs
giraffe: A reticulated giraffe, tall long neck, distinctive brown polygon-patterned coat, short horn-like ossicones, standing on all four legs
okapi: An okapi, dark chocolate-brown body, bold white horizontal stripes on the legs and haunches, giraffe-like head, standing on all four legs
bison: An American bison, massive shaggy brown mane covering the head shoulders and forelegs, large curved horns, standing on all four legs
muskox: A muskox standing on all four legs, with massive horns that meet in the middle of the forehead to form a broad solid helmet-like boss of horn across the brow, then sweep down close beside the head before curving sharply up at the tips. Long shaggy dark brown hair hanging nearly to the ground over short legs. The horns must join across the forehead into a helmet, not rise separately from the sides of the head
moose: A moose standing on all four legs seen from the side, an enormous deer carrying a long horse-like body horizontally on four long legs, with high humped shoulders, a very long heavy drooping muzzle, a dangling flap of skin hanging under the throat, and broad flat palmate antlers. It is a four-legged deer in profile: not standing on two legs, not upright, no human torso, no human arms, no chest or abdominal muscles, absolutely not a humanoid figure
elk: A bull elk standing on all four legs seen from the side, with exactly four legs clearly separated, two front and two back and no extra limbs, a tan body with a dark shaggy brown mane on the neck, and huge sweeping branched antlers curving back over its shoulders
reindeer: A reindeer standing on all four legs, with very large branching antlers sweeping up and back and carrying a distinctive flat forward-pointing brow shovel projecting down over the face, a thick brown-grey coat, a broad blunt muzzle and a stocky build
whitetail: A white-tailed deer standing on all four legs, with a LIGHT coat: pale warm sandy-tan fawn brown, soft and light rather than deep or rusty, shading to a clean white underside, white throat patch and white around the muzzle and eyes, with the broad tail raised to show its bright white underside, and slender antlers. The body colour must be light tawny fawn, not a dark saturated reddish-orange or rust colour
chital: A chital deer, bright rufous coat covered in white spots, branching antlers, standing on all four legs
muntjac: A muntjac, small reddish-brown deer with short spiked antlers, visible facial scent glands, standing on all four legs
pudu: A pudu, the smallest deer in the world: a tiny stocky compact deer standing only knee-high, with a short rounded barrel body, very SHORT stubby legs, a short thick neck, small rounded ears, a blunt rounded face, dense coarse rich reddish-brown fur, and two very short simple unbranched spike antlers barely longer than its ears. Tiny and dumpy, not a slender long-legged deer
gazelle: A Thomson's gazelle, tan body with a bold black side stripe and white belly, ringed lyre-shaped horns, standing on all four legs
springbok: A springbok standing on all four legs, a graceful antelope in three sharp bands of colour: a bright cinnamon-tan back, a bold dark REDDISH-BROWN horizontal stripe running the length of each flank, and a clean white belly and rump below it. Its face is white with a dark chestnut stripe running from each eye down to the muzzle, and it carries black lyre-shaped ridged horns curving up and inward
impala: An impala, sleek reddish-tan body, white underside, lyre-shaped ridged horns, standing on all four legs
gerenuk: A gerenuk, extremely long slender neck and legs, tan body, small head with large eyes, curved horns, standing upright browsing
dikdik: A dik-dik, a miniature antelope no bigger than a hare, with a small rounded body on extremely thin delicate legs, and a distinctive elongated flexible PROBOSCIS snout, a soft mobile trunk-like nose swelling out and drooping over its mouth. Enormous dark eyes each ringed by a bare black preorbital spot, an erect tuft of hair standing up on the forehead between the eyes, and tiny straight spike horns. Grizzled grey-brown with tan legs. Tiny with a swollen flexible nose, not an ordinary gazelle
klipspringer: A klipspringer standing on rock, a very small compact rounded antelope with a thick-set barrel body, an arched back and short sturdy legs, standing up on the very TIPS of its tiny cylindrical hooves like a ballerina on point. Its coat is a coarse grizzled olive-yellow speckled with grey, dense and bristly, with large rounded ears and short straight spike horns. Small compact and rounded up on tiptoe hooves, not a tall slender long-legged deer
kudu: A greater kudu, grey-brown body with thin white vertical stripes, long spiraling ridged horns, standing on all four legs
eland: A common eland, large tan-grey body with faint white stripes, tightly spiraled horns, dewlap hanging from the neck, standing on all four legs
bongo: A bongo antelope, deep chestnut coat with narrow white vertical stripes, long spiralled horns swept back. The body is held horizontal like a deer, with a level back, a long neck and a deer-like head, and four slender legs ending in hooves with all four hooves on the ground. It is an ordinary hoofed animal seen from the side, not humanoid, with no arms, no hands, no muscular chest and no upright posture. Plain empty white background with no grey panel, no box, no backdrop and no ground.
nyala: A male nyala standing on all four legs, with a shaggy dark slate charcoal-brown coat carrying about ten narrow white vertical stripes down the flanks, a long fringe of shaggy hair hanging from the throat, chest and belly, a white chevron between the eyes, and distinctly contrasting bright TAN-ORANGE lower legs below the knees. Long horns with a single open spiral twist tipped with cream-white. The orange lower legs and the shaggy hanging belly fringe are essential
sitatunga: A sitatunga antelope, shaggy brown coat with faint white stripes, elongated splayed hooves, spiralled horns. The body is held horizontal like a deer, with a level back, a long neck and a deer-like head, and four slender legs ending in hooves with all four hooves on the ground. It is an ordinary hoofed animal seen from the side, not humanoid, with no arms, no hands, no muscular chest and no upright posture. Plain empty white background with no grey panel, no box, no backdrop and no ground.
oryx: An Arabian oryx, white body with brown markings on the face and legs, long straight ringed horns, standing on all four legs
saiga: A saiga antelope standing on all four legs, whose defining feature is its NOSE: an enormously enlarged bulbous swollen proboscis, a fleshy inflated trunk-like snout that balloons out above the mouth and droops down over it, with the two nostrils opening downward at the tip, giving it a bizarre puffed-up humped muzzle quite unlike any other antelope. Pale sandy-buff woolly coat, slim legs, and short amber ridged horns rising almost vertically. The huge drooping bulbous nose is the whole point: it must not have the plain straight tapering muzzle of an ordinary sheep, goat or antelope
wildebeest: A blue wildebeest standing on all four legs, its coat a muted slate grey-brown, a dusty ash-grey body faintly marked with darker vertical stripes over the shoulders, a shaggy black mane along the neck, a black beard hanging from the throat, a long dark face and smooth cow-like horns curving out and then up. High shoulders sloping down to lower hindquarters. The colour must be a muted dusty grey-brown, not a bright or saturated blue
hartebeest: A hartebeest, elongated tan face, sloped back, ringed lyre-shaped horns set high on the head, standing on all four legs
topi: A topi standing on all four legs, a slender long-legged antelope with a level back and a narrow lightly-built body, its coat a rich but MUTED reddish-brown with a distinct purplish-black sheen patching the upper forelegs, thighs and face, and pale tan lower legs. Lyre-shaped ridged horns curving up and back. Slim and lightly built like an antelope: the colour must be a deep muted earthy red-brown, not a bright saturated orange-red, and it must not be a heavy muscular bull with a thick neck
blackbuck: A blackbuck, dark brown-black back contrasting with a white belly, long spiraled corkscrew horns, standing on all four legs
pronghorn: A pronghorn, tan and white body with a black face mask, short forked horns, standing on all four legs
bighorn: A bighorn sheep, brown-grey coat, massive tightly curled horns, standing on all four legs
markhor: A markhor standing on all four legs, whose horns are the defining feature: two long horns twisted into tight CORKSCREW SPIRALS, each rising straight up from the head and winding around itself in several full even turns like a helix or a spiral staircase, the two spirals flaring apart from each other in a wide V. Shaggy grey-brown coat with a long flowing white beard hanging from the throat and chest. The horns must be tightly spiralled corkscrews, not smooth curved sweeping ibex or ram horns
takin: A takin, a stocky goat-antelope with a shaggy golden-brown coat, short thick curved horns and a heavy arched snout. The body is held horizontal like a deer, with a level back, a long neck and a deer-like head, and four slender legs ending in hooves with all four hooves on the ground. It is an ordinary hoofed animal seen from the side, not humanoid, with no arms, no hands, no muscular chest and no upright posture. Plain empty white background with no grey panel, no box, no backdrop and no ground.
yak: A wild yak, massive shaggy dark brown-black coat hanging to the ground, thick curved horns, standing on high plateau ground
llama: A llama, long-necked woolly body in cream and brown, banana-shaped ears, standing on all four legs
alpaca: An alpaca, dense fluffy woolly coat, short snout, banana-shaped ears, standing on all four legs
vicuna: A vicuna standing on all four legs, a small slender wild camelid with a very long thin graceful neck, a small delicate head with large eyes and short pointed ears, long slim legs, and a fine woolly coat of pale cinnamon-tan over the back with a distinctive long silky WHITE bib of hair hanging down the chest and a white belly. Plain smooth fur with no buttons, harness, markings or ornaments of any kind on its neck or body
guanaco: A guanaco, tall slender body, reddish-brown wool with a white underside, standing on all four legs
tapir: A Malayan tapir, distinctive body with a black front half and white back half, short flexible trunk-like snout, standing on all four legs
whiterhino: A white rhinoceros standing on all four legs, an immense pale grey rhino with two horns and a very WIDE FLAT SQUARE upper lip, broad and straight across like the mouth of a lawn mower for cropping grass, a long heavy head carried low toward the ground, and a pronounced muscular hump on the back of the neck and shoulders. The broad square lip and the neck hump are essential: its mouth must not be pointed or hooked
blackrhino: A black rhinoceros standing on all four legs, a compact dark grey rhino with two horns, the front one longer, and a distinctly POINTED PREHENSILE upper lip that tapers to a narrow hooked triangular tip curling downward over the mouth for grasping twigs. Its back dips in a pronounced curve between high shoulders and high hips, and its head is carried high. The hooked pointed lip is essential: it must not have a wide flat square mouth
babirusa: A babirusa, a wild PIG with a barrel-shaped pig body on slender legs, sparse bristly grey-brown hide, a long pig snout with a flat round disc nose, and small pig ears. Its defining feature is its extraordinary TUSKS: the upper canines grow straight UP and pierce right through the top of the muzzle, emerging through the skin of the snout and curving back over the face toward the forehead like a pair of horns, while the lower tusks jut up alongside the jaw. It is a pig with tusks growing up through its own snout: it must not be a buffalo, an ox, a wildebeest or any horned cattle
peccary: A collared peccary standing on all four legs, a small compact pig-like animal with a large heavy head that looks big for its short body, slim delicate legs, coarse grizzled salt-and-pepper black-brown bristles, a long pig snout with a flat disc nose, and a distinct pale cream COLLAR band of light bristles running across the shoulders behind the neck like a yoke. Small and compact with almost no tail
chevrotain: A water chevrotain, small deer-like body, reddish-brown coat with white spots and stripes, standing on all four legs
duiker: A common duiker standing on all four legs, a small forest antelope with a warm greyish BROWN coat, tan-brown flanks and a paler cream underside, a dark blaze running down the nose, a small tuft of dark hair on the forehead, and short straight backward-pointing horns. Its body is arched with the hindquarters carried higher than the shoulders in a crouched forest posture. The coat must be a natural earthy grey-brown and tan: it must not be blue, not slate-blue, and not any artificial bright colour
pygmyhippo: A pygmy hippopotamus, small rounded dark grey-black body, standing on all four legs
